hints.title: Post-Order Pruning
hints.text: Process children before deciding whether to delete the parent node so child subtrees can be properly disconnected or promoted.

hints.title: Parent Severing and Child Promotion
hints.text: When a node is deleted, its non-empty surviving children become new independent roots of the remaining forest.

hints.title: Root Candidate Flag
hints.text: Pass a boolean parameter indicating whether the current node is a candidate root, which is true for the initial tree root and whenever a parent was deleted.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def delNodes(self, root: Optional[TreeNode], to_delete: list[int]) -> list[TreeNode]:
        to_del = set(to_delete)
        res = []
        
        def dfs(node, is_root):
            if not node:
                return None
            deleted = node.val in to_del
            if is_root and not deleted:
                res.append(node)
            node.left = dfs(node.left, deleted)
            node.right = dfs(node.right, deleted)
            return None if deleted else node
        
        dfs(root, True)
        return res
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Top-down disconnection without post-order handling complicates child detachment and introduces orphan node tracking issues.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Post-order traversal handles subtree pruning in a single pass using recursion stack space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle child pointers severance by returning null to the parent when deleted.
complexity.notes: All node values in the tree are distinct.
